title: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot improves topology-optimized structure design
summary: A U-Net trained on synthetic preference labels recommended regions for human edits in topology-optimization demonstrations. An L-bracket example had about 39% higher simulated linear buckling load. This validates a design workflow; physical fabrication or load testing was not established by the reviewed material.
ai_technology: Human-in-the-loop AI copilot with topology optimization (machine-learning region-flagging model)

evidence.tested: Computational topology-optimization workflow demonstrations; no separate structural finding established in reviewed scope.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed demonstrations are computational; they do not establish physical load-test performance or in-service structural outcomes. Compliance and timing comparisons differ between the article text, table and abstract and were not reconciled in this review. The training preferences were synthetic, and users modified the recommended regions.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning model quickly identifies design regions a human would likely want to change, within a topology optimization workflow.

source_review.scope: Primary journal PDF Results, Methods, Table 1 and Discussion; indexed publisher publication metadata. Reviewed results concern computational topology-optimization demonstrations and simulated linear buckling.
